lines.gloss: Mind-preceded [are] dhammas (things/states);

witness_glosses.zh: Mind is the root/basis of dharmas (things).
witness_glosses.bo: Mind goes before dharmas.

differences.note: 心為法本 'mind is the root of dharmas': 本 'root/basis' renders pubbaṅgama 'going before' loosely; same idea of mind's primacy.

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses agree in sense; the English for dhammā (states / things / experiences / phenomena) must be fixed once for the book.

lines.gloss: mind [is their] chief, [they are] made of mind;

witness_glosses.pd: mind [is their] chief, [they are] swift as mind (manojavā);
witness_glosses.zh: mind is honoured, mind is the one that commands/sends (心使);
witness_glosses.bo: mind is swift; mind is the chief.

differences.note: Pāli manomayā 'made of mind' stands alone against manojavā 'swift as mind' in Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan (ཡིད་མགྱོགས 'mind is swift').
心尊心使 'mind honoured, mind commanding' does not clearly render either manomaya or manojava; it cannot be counted for either side.
Tibetan puts 'swift' before 'chief' within the line; order only.

lines.tier_reason: A real difference of sense where Pāli alone (not even Patna) has manomayā against every other Indic witness; choosing 'made of mind' or 'swift as mind' for the opening of the book needs its own judgment (T4 decision 'manomaya-manojava').

lines.gloss: If with a corrupted mind

witness_glosses.zh: [if] within the heart one thinks evil
witness_glosses.bo: If with a very malicious mind

differences.note: Gāndhārī and Sanskrit have hi 'for/indeed' where Pāli has ce 'if' (Patna ca is the usual Patna spelling of 'if'); Tibetan གལ་ཏེ supports 'if'. Conditional vs general statement; same sense.
中心念惡 'in the heart thinks evil' renders 'corrupted mind' as thinking evil.
རབ་གདུག་པ 'very malicious/poisonous' for praduṣṭa 'corrupted'.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense in all; ce/hi is grammar-neutral, but paduṭṭha/pasanna (corrupted/clear mind) is a recurring pair whose English should be fixed once.

lines.gloss: one speaks or acts,

witness_glosses.bo: whether one has spoken or else has acted

differences.note: Gāndhārī bhaṣadi va karodi va: one 'va' is italic in the edition (marked uncertain); no change of sense.

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses agree.

lines.gloss: from that suffering follows him,

witness_glosses.zh: offence and suffering pursue [him] of themselves
witness_glosses.bo: by that, he obtains suffering

differences.note: 罪苦 'offence and suffering' adds 罪 'guilt/offence'; 自追 'pursue of themselves' = anveti.
འཐོབ 'obtains' for anveti 'follows'; the image of following is weakened but the sense (suffering results) is the same.

lines.tier_reason: Agreement in sense; dukkha (suffering/pain) is a book-wide rendering.

lines.gloss: like the wheel [follows] the foot of the one who draws (the draught ox).

witness_glosses.ga: like the wheel ... of the drawer, on the road (pathi?) — reading uncertain
witness_glosses.zh: the cart rolls/crushes in the rut
witness_glosses.bo: like a wheel cutting off a head

differences.note: Tibetan འཁོར་ལོས་མགོ་བོ་བཅད་པ་བཞིན 'like a wheel cutting off a head' is a different simile from its own Sanskrit source (cakraṁ vā vahataḥ padam); the witness note calls it recensional.
Gāndhārī vahaṇe pathi: pathi may be a locative 'on the road/track' rather than padaṁ 'foot'; I cannot parse it securely. Image of wheel following the draught animal is kept.
車轢于轍 'the cart crushes [along] in the rut' keeps the cart-wheel image without the ox's foot.

lines.tier_reason: Sanskrit, Patna, Pāli agree; the Tibetan simile is a lone departure from its own Sanskrit original and the Gāndhārī wording is unclear, both settled by general rules.

verses.notes: Line 2 is the major crux (manomayā vs manojavā). The final simile needs a supplied ⟨ox⟩ in English (vahato 'of the one drawing'). Edition 'ins' marks in Sanskrit lines 2 and 6 (e.g. on 'ḥ', '//') look like revision markup and carry no textual weight.

lines.gloss: Mind-preceded [are] dhammas;

witness_glosses.zh: Mind is the root of dharmas.
witness_glosses.bo: Mind goes before dharmas.

differences.note: As verse 1.

lines.tier_reason: Identical to verse 1 line 1; dhammā rendering.

lines.gloss: mind [is their] chief, [they are] made of mind;

witness_glosses.bo: mind is swift; mind is the chief

differences.note: As verse 1: manomayā (Pāli alone) vs manojavā (all other Indic witnesses and Tibetan).

lines.tier_reason: Same crux as verse 1 line 2; one decision covers both.

lines.gloss: If with a clear (bright, trusting) mind

witness_glosses.zh: [if] within the heart one thinks good
witness_glosses.bo: If with a very clear (faithful) mind

differences.note: hi 'for' vs ce 'if', as in verse 1.
念善 'thinks good' renders pasanna as goodness of thought rather than clarity/confidence.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense; pasanna needs a fixed rendering (clear / serene / confident).

lines.gloss: one speaks or acts,
lines.tier_reason: All agree.

lines.gloss: from that happiness follows him,

witness_glosses.zh: merit/blessing and joy pursue [him] of themselves
witness_glosses.bo: by that, he obtains happiness

differences.note: 福樂 'blessing and joy' adds 福 'merit/blessing'.
'obtains' for 'follows', as verse 1.

lines.tier_reason: Agreement; sukha paired with dukkha needs a fixed rendering.

lines.gloss: like a shadow that does not depart.

witness_glosses.sa: like a shadow that indeed follows
witness_glosses.zh: like a shadow following the body/form
witness_glosses.bo: like a shadow that follows after

differences.note: Pāli and Patna anapāyinī 'not departing' vs anugāminī 'following' in Gāndhārī and Sanskrit, with Chinese 隨 and Tibetan རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བ 'following'; same image, different word.
如影隨形 adds 形 'the form/body' that the shadow follows.

lines.tier_reason: Same idea, different word: Pāli+Patna 'never leaving' against all others' 'following'; settled once by the wording default (a majority of lineages here actually favours 'following').

verses.notes: Shares verse 1's crux. Final simile: anapāyinī vs anugāminī is a wording split in which Pāli+Patna stand against Gāndhārī, Udānavarga and Chinese; flag for the wording-default ruling.

lines.gloss: 'He abused me, he struck me,

witness_glosses.bo: '[They] spoke harshly to me, [they] reviled [me]' (parse uncertain)

differences.note: Sanskrit avocan 'they spoke' replaces avadhi 'he struck'; Tibetan has two verbs of speech (ཁ་ཟེར་བ, གཤེ), so the Udānavarga line has verbal abuse only, no striking.
Sanskrit verbs are 3rd plural (ākrośan, avocan, ajayan) against Pāli/Patna 3rd singular; Tibetan marks plural with དག.
T212 人若罵我 'if someone reviles me' renders only the first verb, as a condition.

lines.tier_reason: A two-voice split, Pāli+Patna (struck, singular) against the Udānavarga line (spoke, plural); Gāndhārī is absent and the Chinese is too compressed to decide, so a lineage rule settles it.

lines.gloss: he defeated me, he robbed me' —

witness_glosses.sa: they defeated me, he/they made [me] lose (ajāpayet)
witness_glosses.bo: 'I was defeated, [they] caused my defeat/loss' — thus

differences.note: ahāsi 'robbed' vs ajāpayet 'caused [me] to lose' (causative of ji/jyā); Tibetan ཕམ་བྱེད 'caused defeat/loss'. Close in sense (loss of goods vs being worsted).
Plural subject in the Udānavarga line, as in line 1.
勝我不勝 'defeated me, I did not win' (T212 commentary glosses it as winning or not by the Dharma); robbery is absent.
Tibetan ends the quoted complaint with ཞེས 'thus', marking lines 1-2 as a quotation.

lines.tier_reason: Part of the same Pāli+Patna vs Udānavarga split (number, robbery vs causing loss); Chinese paraphrase; settled with line 1.

lines.gloss: and those who bind themselves to that,

witness_glosses.pd: those who bind themselves to those [things]
witness_glosses.sa: those who here bind themselves [to it]
witness_glosses.zh: those who follow [it] gratifying their feelings
witness_glosses.bo: whoever holds this in mind

differences.note: Patna tāni 'those (things)' plural object for Pāli taṁ 'that'.
Sanskrit atra 'here/in this' for ca taṁ.
快意從者 'those who follow with gratified feeling'; T212's commentary explains it as those who keep thinking this way and so increase enmity: same sense, freely put.

lines.tier_reason: All carry 'those who harbour it'; differences are grammar and Chinese idiom.

lines.gloss: their hostility does not cease.

witness_glosses.bo: his/their grudge does not become pacified

differences.note: 怨終不息 'resentment in the end does not cease'.
Tibetan དེ་ཡི 'his' singular possessor.

lines.tier_reason: Agreement; vera (hostility/enmity/hatred) needs a book-wide rendering.

verses.notes: Gāndhārī not located. The Chinese is T212 (T210 lacks this verse). The Sanskrit lines 1-2 carry 'ins' marks in the edition on 'm avocan mām' and 'ajayan mām a'/'e'; I take these as revision markup, but if they mark editorial restoration the Sanskrit 'avocan' would be weaker. Patna is 3rd singular like Pāli.

lines.gloss: 'He abused me, he struck me,

witness_glosses.bo: '[They] spoke harshly to me, [they] reviled [me]'

differences.note: As verse 3 line 1: spoke vs struck; plural.
T213 若人致毀罵 'if someone heaps abuse' (partial parallel, listed for both 3 and 4).

lines.tier_reason: Same split as verse 3 line 1, settled by the same rule.

lines.gloss: he defeated me, he robbed me' —

witness_glosses.zh: he won, I did not win
witness_glosses.bo: 'I was defeated, [they] caused my defeat' — thus

differences.note: As verse 3 line 2.
T213 彼勝我不勝 'he won, I did not win'; robbery absent.

lines.tier_reason: As verse 3 line 2.

lines.gloss: but those who do not bind themselves to that,

witness_glosses.zh: one who follows [his] thought with happiness (no negation)
witness_glosses.bo: whoever does not hold this in mind

differences.note: T213 快樂從意者 has no negative; it is not the Pāli's 'do not harbour' and is unclear (it may mean one who follows a contented mind). Partial parallel only.

lines.tier_reason: All full witnesses agree on the negative; only the partial Chinese lacks it, which the partial-parallel rule settles.

lines.gloss: in them hostility ceases.

witness_glosses.bo: his grudge becomes pacified

differences.note: T213 怨終得休息 'resentment finally comes to rest'.

lines.tier_reason: Agreement; vera rendering.

verses.notes: Gāndhārī not located. The Chinese T213 stanza is a single 'positive' stanza used for both 3 and 4; it is a partial parallel.

lines.gloss: For not by hostility [do] hostilities

witness_glosses.zh: one who is angry at the resentful/resentment
witness_glosses.bo: here, by enmity, those with enmity

differences.note: 慍於怨者 'one who is angry at resentment' recasts the abstract statement as a person; same sense.
འཁོན་ཅན་དག 'those having enmity' (persons) for vairāṇi 'hostilities'; Tibetan moves 'here' (iha) to this line.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense; vera rendering.

lines.gloss: ever cease here;

witness_glosses.bo: never become pacified

differences.note: 未甞無怨 'has never been free of resentment': negative statement kept.

lines.tier_reason: All agree.

lines.gloss: and by non-hostility they cease:

witness_glosses.bo: by patience enmity becomes pacified

differences.note: Sanskrit kṣāntyā and Tibetan བཟོད་པས 'by patience' against avera 'non-hostility' in Pāli and Patna; Chinese 不慍 'not being angry' sides with avera (T212/T213 have 行忍 'practising patience', following their Udānavarga source).

lines.tier_reason: Udānavarga line (Sanskrit+Tibetan as one voice, with T212/T213) against Pāli, Patna and T210; a lineage rule settles it.

lines.gloss: this is the age-old/eternal law (dhamma).

witness_glosses.zh: this Way can be taken as the principle
witness_glosses.bo: this is the nature of dharma(s)

differences.note: 是道可宗 'this Way is to be taken as authoritative': 道 for dhamma, and no word for sanantano.
ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན 'the nature of dharma' renders sanātana as 'nature' rather than 'eternal'.
sanātano/sanātanaḥ: normal form; Pāli sanantano metri causa.

lines.tier_reason: Same idea across witnesses, but both dhammo and sanantano need book-wide renderings (the method names sanantano explicitly).

verses.notes: Gāndhārī not located. Patna places this in its Khānti (patience) chapter yet reads avereṇa, not patience.

lines.gloss: Others do not understand

witness_glosses.zh: do not be fond of blaming others
witness_glosses.bo: because the others do not understand

differences.note: T210 不好責彼 'do not like to blame others': only 彼 'others' overlaps; the admonition differs.
Tibetan ཕ་རོལ་པོ་དག་མི་ཤེས་པས 'since the others do not understand' (third line of a related six-line stanza).

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna (the only full witnesses) agree and the partial Tibetan agrees; the partial Chinese has a different admonition, which the partial-parallel rule sets aside.

lines.gloss: that we here must restrain ourselves / come to an end (yamāmase).

witness_glosses.pd: we here are winning/must strive to win (jayāmatha)
witness_glosses.bo: I strive at this

differences.note: Patna jayāmatha 'we conquer / strive to win' for yamāmase.
Chinese 務自省身 'strive to examine oneself' and Tibetan བདག་ནི་འདི་ལ་བརྩོན་པར་བྱེད 'I strive at this' both read a sense of exertion/self-restraint, not of perishing.

lines.tier_reason: yamāmase is ambiguous (restrain ourselves / exert ourselves / perish); Patna reads differently and the partial parallels lean to exertion; the reading needs its own judgment (T4 decision 'yamamase').

lines.gloss: but those there who understand,

witness_glosses.bo: whoever here are wise

differences.note: Tibetan མཁས་པ 'the wise' for 'those who understand'.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna agree; partials agree in sense.

lines.gloss: from that their quarrels cease.

witness_glosses.bo: they are pacified by gentle words

differences.note: 永滅無患 'forever extinguished, free of trouble'.
དེ་དག་བཞམས་པའི་ཚིག་གིས་ཞི 'they are calmed by gentle words': a different subject and means.
medhakā for medhagā.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli and Patna agree, but medhaga 'quarrels' is a rare word and the partial parallels diverge; partial-parallel rule applies and the word needs a fixed sense.

extra.note: Tibetan partial (Uv 14.8 Tib.): opening address with no Pāli counterpart.

extra.gloss: one who strives/contends with talk (ཁ་བྱ; parse uncertain).
extra.note: No Pāli counterpart; meaning of ཁ་བྱ uncertain to me.

verses.notes: Sanskrit and Gāndhārī not located. Chinese and Tibetan are partial/provisional parallels (the Tibetan note says Rockhill does not identify it with Dhp 6). Only Pāli and Patna are full witnesses.

lines.gloss: One who dwells contemplating the attractive,

witness_glosses.zh: in practice seeing the body as pure
witness_glosses.bo: who dwells viewing [things] as pure

differences.note: Sanskrit nityam 'constantly' for viharantaṁ 'dwelling'; Tibetan གནས་བྱེད་པ 'dwells' sides with Pāli.
行見身淨 adds 身 'the body' as the object of the 'beautiful' view.
Tibetan places this line fourth.
གཙང་བ / 淨 'pure, clean' for śubha 'attractive, beautiful'.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense; subha/asubha needs a book-wide rendering (attractive/beautiful/pure).

lines.gloss: unrestrained in the faculties,

witness_glosses.bo: whoever is unrestrained in the faculties

differences.note: Tibetan first line.

lines.tier_reason: All agree; indriya (faculties/senses) needs a fixed rendering.

lines.gloss: and immoderate in eating,

witness_glosses.zh: not moderate in food and drink
witness_glosses.bo: and not knowing the measure of food

lines.tier_reason: All agree.

lines.gloss: lazy, of low energy —

witness_glosses.bo: of lapsed mindfulness and lazy

differences.note: Sanskrit hīnaṁ jāgarikāsu ca 'deficient in wakefulness' replaces 'lazy, low in energy'.
Tibetan དྲན་པ་ཉམས་དང་ལེ་ལོ་ཅན 'mindfulness lapsed and lazy': mixes a wakefulness/mindfulness item with laziness.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli, Patna, Gāndhārī and Chinese agree; the Udānavarga line differs, settled by the one-voice rule.

lines.gloss: him indeed Māra overpowers,

witness_glosses.zh: he is controlled by the deviant/evil (邪)
witness_glosses.bo: he is overcome by passions

differences.note: Gāndhārī raku, Sanskrit rāgo and Tibetan འདོད་ཆགས 'passion' against Māra in Pāli and Patna.
為邪所制 'controlled by the deviant': 邪 can stand for Māra ('the evil one') or for wrong desire; cannot be counted securely.

lines.tier_reason: Two lineages (Pāli+Patna) against two (Gāndhārī, Udānavarga) on the agent, Māra or passion; a best-reading judgment (T4 decision 'mara-raga').

lines.gloss: as the wind a weak tree.

witness_glosses.bo: like an unstable tree by the wind

differences.note: 如風靡草 'as wind bends the grass': native idiom with grass for tree.
abalam 'strengthless' = dubbalaṁ.

lines.tier_reason: All Indic and Tibetan agree; the Chinese changes the simile's object (grass), which the Chinese-free-rendering rule settles.

verses.notes: Tibetan reorders: faculties, food, mindfulness/laziness, viewing-as-pure, passion, tree. Crux: Māra (Pāli, Patna) vs passion (Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan). Sanskrit 'ins' mark on 'h' in 'hīnaṁ' taken as revision markup.

lines.gloss: One who dwells contemplating the unattractive,

witness_glosses.bo: who dwells by viewing the impure

differences.note: nityam for viharantaṁ, as verse 7.
觀身不淨 'contemplates the body as impure' (body explicit).
Tibetan fourth line.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense; subha/asubha rendering.

lines.gloss: well restrained in the faculties,

witness_glosses.bo: whoever is well restrained in the faculties

differences.note: sisavudu for susaṁvuta.

lines.tier_reason: All agree; indriya rendering.

lines.gloss: and moderate in eating,

witness_glosses.bo: and knowing the measure of food

differences.note: Patna is broken after mā... (fragmentary), consistent with Pāli.

lines.tier_reason: All agree (Patna fragmentary but consistent).

lines.gloss: faithful, of aroused energy —

witness_glosses.bo: mindful and endowed with energy

differences.note: Sanskrit yuktaṁ jāgarikāsu ca 'devoted to wakefulness' replaces faith and energy.
Tibetan སོ་སོར་དྲན 'mindful' + བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ལྡན 'energetic': no faith.
常樂精進 'always delighting in effort': energy kept, faith (saddhā) absent.
Patna ...ddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ is damaged at the start but consistent with saddhaṁ.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli, Gāndhārī (and damaged Patna) have faith+energy; Udānavarga differs (one voice) and the Chinese drops faith; rules settle it.

lines.gloss: him indeed Māra does not overpower,

witness_glosses.zh: he is not moved by the deviant
witness_glosses.bo: he is not overcome by passion

differences.note: Passion vs Māra, as verse 7 line 5.
Sanskrit lacks vai/ve 'indeed' here.

lines.tier_reason: Same crux as verse 7 line 5; one decision covers both.

lines.gloss: as the wind [does not overpower] a rocky mountain.

witness_glosses.sa: as the wind a firm rock
witness_glosses.bo: like a mountain not moved by wind

differences.note: śailam iva sthiram 'a firm rock' for selaṁ pabbataṁ 'a rock mountain'.
མི་གཡོས 'unmoved' makes the negation explicit.

lines.tier_reason: All witnesses carry the same image of wind failing against a mountain/rock.

verses.notes: Patna fragmentary (lines 3-4). Same Māra/passion crux as verse 7.

lines.gloss: One not free of stain (kasāva), the stained (ochre) robe (kāsāva)

witness_glosses.bo: whoever, while still having dregs (impurities)

differences.note: 不吐毒態 'not vomiting out poisonous attitudes': kaṣāya taken as 'poison/astringent', with 'vomit' from the paired verse's vanta; the pun is lost.
སྙིགས་མ 'dregs, impurity' for kaṣāya; the robe word is in line 2, so the pun is lost.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense in all Indic witnesses; the kasāva/kāsāva wordplay needs a once-only decision on how to render it in English.

lines.gloss: who will put on [that] cloth,

witness_glosses.bo: wears the saffron robe

differences.note: Chinese has no line about putting on the robe; its second line 欲心馳騁 is extra (see extra).

lines.tier_reason: All Indic and Tibetan agree; the Chinese omits the line and replaces it, settled by the Chinese-free-rendering rule.

lines.gloss: devoid of self-control and truth,

witness_glosses.zh: not yet able to tame oneself
witness_glosses.bo: he who lacks taming and gentleness

differences.note: damasacca 'restraint and truth' (Pāli, Patna) against dama-sorata/sauratya 'restraint and gentleness' (Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan དེས་པ).
未能自調 'not able to tame oneself' renders only dama.

lines.tier_reason: Pāli+Patna against Gāndhārī and the Udānavarga line on 'truth' vs 'gentleness'; a best-reading judgment (T4 decision 'sacca-sorata').

lines.gloss: he does not deserve the ochre robe.

witness_glosses.zh: is not fit for the Dharma robe
witness_glosses.bo: is not worthy of wearing the saffron

differences.note: 法衣 'Dharma robe' for kāsāva.

lines.tier_reason: All agree; the robe word belongs to the kasāva pun ruling.

extra.note: Chinese line with no Pāli counterpart, in place of 'who will put on the robe'.

verses.notes: Wordplay verse. Crux: sacca vs sorata (shared with verse 10).

lines.gloss: But one who would have vomited out the stains,

witness_glosses.sa: but one who would be one who has vomited the stains
witness_glosses.zh: able to spit out poisonous states
witness_glosses.bo: whoever, having abandoned the impurities

differences.note: Sanskrit vāntakaṣāyaḥ syāt shows Pāli -assa is the optative 'would be' (not a genitive).
སྤངས 'abandoned' for vānta 'vomited'.
能吐毒態 'able to spit out poisonous states'.

lines.tier_reason: Same sense; the kasāva pun ruling applies.

lines.gloss: well composed in virtues (sīla),

witness_glosses.zh: in the precepts, the mind calm
witness_glosses.bo: well composed in ethical discipline

differences.note: śīlehi instrumental 'by/through virtues' for locative sīlesu.

candidates.label: dhamma-rendering
candidates.statement: Fix the English for dhamma by sense class, once for the book: (a) plural dhammā as the objects of mind (1.1, 2.1); (b) dhamma as 'law/principle/the way things are' in 5.4; (c) dhamma as 'the Teaching' in 20.2. The Chinese 法/道 and Tibetan ཆོས render the same Indic word and count as agreement.
candidates.recommendation: (a) 'things' or 'states' (not 'experiences', which adds an interpretation); (b) 'law' with sanantano per its own ruling; (c) 'the Teaching' (or 'Dhamma' capitalised if the book keeps the word).

candidates.label: sanantano
candidates.statement: How to render sanantano/sanātana 'from of old, perpetual' in 5.4. The Tibetan renders it as 'the nature (རང་བཞིན) of dharma' and the Chinese gives no 'eternal' word (是道可宗), so neither witness asserts eternity.
candidates.recommendation: 'age-old' (or 'ancient'): literal to 'from of old' and imports no metaphysics.

candidates.label: vera-avera
candidates.statement: Fix the English for vera/vaira (and avera) throughout: Chinese 怨 'resentment' and Tibetan འཁོན 'grudge, enmity' support a relational sense.

candidates.label: kasava-pun
candidates.statement: Verses 9-10 pun on kasāva 'stain, impurity' and kāsāva 'the ochre (stained/dyed) robe'. Literal+ allows a departure to keep the poetic quality; decide once how to render it.
options: Keep the pun: 'stain' / 'the stained robe' (with ⟨ochre⟩ or ⟨saffron⟩ as needed)
'dye' pun: 'not free of the dye of defilement ... the dyed robe'
candidates.recommendation: Keep the pun with stain/stained and ⟨ochre⟩ supplied once; render 'vomited out' literally in 10.1.

candidates.label: core-glossary
candidates.statement: A book-wide glossary for recurring terms that appear in this chapter and that every witness agrees on in sense but which have more than one plausible English: paduṭṭha/pasanna (1.3, 2.3), dukkha/sukha (1.5, 2.5), subha/asubha (7.1, 8.1), indriya (7.2, 8.2), sīla (10.2), sāra/asāra (11-12), saṅkappa (11.4, 12.4), medhaga (6.4), rāga/dosa/moha (13.4, 14.4, 20.3), puñña/pāpa (15-18), tappati (17.1-2), duggati/suggati (17.4, 18.4), pamatta (19.2), samaṇa/sāmañña (19.4, 20.6).
options: Proposed: corrupted/clear mind; suffering/happiness; attractive/unattractive; faculties; virtue (or ethical conduct); essential/inessential (or 'the core'); intention; quarrels; passion/hatred/delusion; merit/evil; tormented; bad/good destination; heedless; recluse/recluse's life

Alternatives: corrupt/serene; pain/pleasure; beautiful/foul; senses; precepts; heartwood/what is not heartwood; thought/resolve; lust/aversion/confusion; good deeds/bad deeds; burns (with remorse); hell/heaven (interpretive, not literal); negligent; ascetic/contemplative
candidates.recommendation: Approve the first row as defaults, each reviewable term by term; do not use the interpretive alternatives (e.g. 'hell/heaven').

candidates.label: same-sense-wording-default
candidates.statement: Default for 'same idea, different word' splits: when witnesses carry the same image or idea in different words (e.g. anapāyinī 'never leaving' vs anugāminī 'following' 2.6; viharantaṁ vs nityam 7.1/8.1; dassino vs saññino 11.2; vijjhati vs bhindati 13-14; modati vs nandati 16), the Blend renders the Pāli word, unless a clear majority of independent lineages has another word and that word reads better.
options: Render the Pāli wording unless the majority differs and reads better (case flagged)
candidates.recommendation: Third option; in this chapter it would flag only 2.6 ('like a shadow that follows' has Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan and Chinese against Pāli+Patna).

candidates.label: uv-one-voice
candidates.statement: The Sanskrit Udānavarga and its Tibetan translation count as one voice. Where that voice alone differs in sense from the other lineages (Pāli, Patna, Gāndhārī, Chinese), the Blend follows the others and records the Udānavarga variant. Where the Tibetan alone departs from its Sanskrit source (e.g. 1.6 'a wheel cutting off a head'), it is treated as a matter of Tibetan translation or recension and not followed. Where the split is Pāli+Patna against the Udānavarga only, with Gāndhārī absent and the Chinese undecided (3.1-2, 4.1-2), the Pāli+Patna reading stands.
options: Adopt but treat Pāli+Patna vs Udānavarga-only splits as T4

candidates.label: single-or-fragmentary-witness
candidates.statement: A single witness differing alone against the agreement of the others (e.g. Gāndhārī 'unguarded/well guarded' for 'undeveloped/well developed' 13.3, 14.3; an unparsable Gāndhārī word 1.6; Patna's added epithets 20.4) is recorded but not followed. A fragmentary witness never carries a reading alone, though it may confirm one (Patna 8.3-4, 16.3).
options: Adopt but exempt the Gāndhārī (as the oldest manuscript) so its lone readings go to T4

candidates.label: chinese-free-rendering
candidates.statement: The Chinese (T210, fallbacks T212/T213) counts as agreement when it renders the same Indic sense in native words (心 for mind, 道/法 for dhamma, 罪/福 additions). Where it recasts an image or line (grass for tree 7.6; no robe-donning line 9.2; herd of cattle 19.3; 'not a disciple of the Buddha'), drops an item (faith 8.4), or adds lines (9, 19), it informs but does not replace the Indic agreement; such lines are T3 under this rule.
options: Adopt and also allow the Chinese to decide two-against-two Indic splits
candidates.recommendation: Adopt; let the Chinese count in splits only where it clearly renders one side.

candidates.label: partial-or-absent-parallels
candidates.statement: Partial or provisional parallels (Chinese T213 at 3-4; Chinese and Tibetan at 6) and witnesses that lack a line (Udānavarga and Gāndhārī lines missing at 20.3-5; Chinese/Tibetan restructuring at 17-18) inform but do not supply or remove a line. A Pāli line that other witnesses simply lack is kept, resting on Pāli (and any agreeing witness); where Pāli is the only Indic witness (17-18), Pāli supplies the line and the Chinese/Tibetan only inform.
options: Adopt, but drop or bracket Pāli-only lines that every other witness lacks
candidates.recommendation: Adopt (keep all 423 Pāli positions line for line, as the scope requires).

candidates.label: lineage-majority-default
candidates.statement: Optional general default for the chapter's Indic cruxes, offered so the owner can decide whether these should be ruled once or decided one by one: when Pāli (alone or with Patna) stands against Gāndhārī and/or the Udānavarga line on a sense-bearing word (manomayā/manojavā 1.2, 2.2; Māra/rāga 7.5, 8.5; sacca/sorata 9.3, 10.3; sāmañña/śrāmaṇyārtha 19.4, 20.6), the Blend either keeps Pāli, or follows the majority of independent lineages (counting Pāli+Patna as close kin and Sanskrit+Tibetan as one).
options: No blanket rule: decide each as a T4 (current tiering)
Keep the Pāli reading in all such cases (base-text rule)
Follow the majority of independent lineages (would give 'swift as mind', and leaves 2-2 splits as T4)
candidates.recommendation: No blanket rule for chapter 1: these are few, prominent and individually arguable, so keep them as T4; revisit after chapter 1 if the pattern recurs often.

t4_decisions.label: manomaya-manojava
t4_decisions.question: Pāli manomayā 'made of mind' (Pāli alone) or manojavā 'swift as mind' (Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan)?
options: Keep Pāli: 'mind is their chief, they are made of mind'
Follow the other witnesses: 'mind is their chief, swift as mind' (or 'mind is chief, mind is swift')
t4_decisions.lean: Open. The 'all other witnesses' reading is strong evidence; keeping Pāli matches the book's base text.

t4_decisions.label: yamamase
t4_decisions.question: Sense of yamāmase (Patna jayāmatha).
options: 'that we here must restrain ourselves' (backed loosely by the partial Chinese/Tibetan 'strive')
'that here we are coming to our end' (perish)
t4_decisions.lean: 'restrain ourselves' fits the partial parallels' 'strive/examine oneself' best.

t4_decisions.label: mara-raga
t4_decisions.question: Agent: Māra (Pāli, Patna) or passion (Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan)?
t4_decisions.lean: Open; two lineages each; Gāndhārī is oldest.

t4_decisions.label: sacca-sorata
t4_decisions.question: damasacca 'restraint and truth' (Pāli, Patna) or dama-sorata 'restraint and gentleness' (Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan)?

t4_decisions.label: samanna-attha
t4_decisions.question: 'sharer in the recluse's state' (Pāli, Patna) or 'sharer in the goal of recluseship' (Gāndhārī, Sanskrit)?
options: 'has no share in the recluse's life'
'has no share in the goal of the recluse's life'
